Definition: of Hebrew origin (H1162); Booz, (i.e. Boaz), an Israelite:--Booz.
BiblicalUsage: Booz is the Greek form of Boaz, the kinsman-redeemer of Ruth and the ancestor of David. In Matthew 1:5 Salmon begat Booz of Rachab, and Booz begat Obed of Ruth, in the genealogy of Jesus. In Luke 3:32 Booz stands in the same line, the son of Salmon, in the genealogy that runs back to Adam. The Greek text spells the name Βόες, a different form from the dictionary spelling, but it is the same man. For his story, see the study on Boaz.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Greek spelling changes nothing: the redeemer of Ruth is in the line of Christ, by whatever letters his name is written.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
